questions.knowledge_point: Differentiating a General Exponential Function Using the Chain Rule
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={2}^{u},\,u=9x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}={2}^{u}\operatorname{ln}⁡2,\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=9.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={2}^{u}\operatorname{ln}⁡2\cdot 9 \\  & =9\operatorname{ln}⁡2\cdot {2}^{u} \\  & =9\operatorname{ln}⁡2\cdot {2}^{9x}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Differentiating an Exponential Function with a Nonlinear Exponent
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

$$
f={e}^{u},\,u={x}^{2}.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}={e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{u}\cdot (2x) \\  & =2x{e}^{u} \\  & =2x{e}^{{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Differentiating a General Exponential Function Using the Chain Rule
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

$$
f={3}^{u},\,u=2{x}^{2}.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}={3}^{u}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3),\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=4x.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={3}^{u}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)\cdot (4x) \\  & =4x\cdot {3}^{u}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) \\  & =4x\cdot {3}^{2{x}^{2}}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y={e}^{3{x}^{2}-3}$ at the point where $x=-1.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={e}^{u},\,u=3{x}^{2}-3.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}={e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6x.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{u}\cdot 6x \\  & =6x\cdot {e}^{u} \\  & =6x{e}^{3{x}^{2}-3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope of the tangent to the curve at $x=-1$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-1} & ={6x{e}^{3{x}^{2}-3}|}_{x=-1} \\  & =6(-1){e}^{3(-1)^{2}-3} \\  & =-6\cdot {e}^{0} \\  & =-6\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Differentiating an Exponential Function with a Nonlinear Exponent
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

$$
f={e}^{u},\,u=4{x}^{5}.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}={e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=20{x}^{4}.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{u}\cdot (20{x}^{4}) \\  & =20{x}^{4}{e}^{u} \\  & =20{x}^{4}{e}^{4{x}^{5}}.\end{aligned}
$$
